Check: Each requirement has a unique ID, one statement, one owner
Each requirement is atomic, testable and unambiguous
Each requirement has acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then or measurable)
Each requirement is classified (business, stakeholder, solution, transition) and prioritised (MoSCoW)
Each requirement traces to an objective, a component, a data entity and a test
No requirement names a product unless a constraint is approved
Terms are defined once in the glossary and used consistently
Stakeholders are identified with concerns and engagement approach
Business rules are separate from process steps and numbered
Every data entity has an owner, steward, classification and retention
Every mandatory attribute has a data-quality rule
Every interface has an owner, direction, mode, frequency and classification
Decisions are recorded as ADRs with options and rationale
Security, privacy and residency reviewed against NFRs
Risks have owner, score and mitigation
Assumptions and dependencies listed with fall-backs
Requirements verified (peer review) and validated (stakeholder sign-off)
Placeholders in [brackets] are either filled or listed as open items
Change requests assessed for impact on scope, data, cost and risk
Client, vendor and personal details are absent from reference artefacts
